name: [Portal] Move Merchant Access from the portal root to its own page and menu item
description:
### Summary

 was written against the Partner Portal root: the shop list would render inside `PartnerPortalOverview`, the portal's single existing admin page, which today still carries a placeholder React body. This task gives the list a page of its own — a new `cms2_admin_section_map` row as a child of the „Portál partnera" row, localized slugs for cs/sk/en/hu/de, the menu item „Obchody", and a matching controller plus Inertia React page registered everywhere admin routing requires. The portal menu stays deliberately shallow: one level of children under „Portál partnera", no deeper nesting. The dedicated portal shell from the design — its own branded header and the four-item sidebar — is explicitly out of scope and belongs to follow-up tasks. One non-obvious prerequisite is included: the parent row's id must be added to the hardcoded submenu allowlist in `navigation.tpl`, or the new item renders nowhere. Columns, data source and shop hand-off stay in  and .

### Why?

The Partner Portal owns exactly one admin page, so  had nowhere to put the shop table except the portal root. That makes the landing page do two jobs, leaves the list without a URL to link or bookmark, and blocks  from extending the same screen with role context, search and sorting. Splitting the page out now, before either task is implemented, is cheaper than splitting it afterwards, and it forces the slug decision to be taken once and deliberately rather than invented inside a feature PR — `cms2_admin_section_map_lng` enforces `UNIQUE (language, indexName)`, so slugs are a global namespace. Doing it as its own task also surfaces the submenu allowlist, which is the kind of hardcoded detail that silently eats half a day when discovered mid-feature.

### What?

A partner working in the admin sees „Portál partnera" in the sidebar with „Obchody" nested underneath it. Selecting „Obchody" opens a page headed „Vstup do obchodů" at its own localized URL. On delivery of this task the page is an empty shell that  then fills with the table; the portal root keeps its own identity and does not carry the shop list. The item is hidden whenever the `partnerPortal` module is inactive, exactly like the existing portal page. No existing section is re-parented, no third level is introduced, and the portal keeps using the standard admin layout — the branded portal shell in the design is a later task.

### Open questions

- Slug wording: page-derived (`vstup-do-obchodu`, matching the H1) or menu-derived (`obchody`, matching the sidebar label)? `obchody` is free but is a generic word another team may plausibly want, and slugs are a global per-language namespace; recommendation is page-derived. Partnership to confirm cs/sk/hu wording.
- Is `de` in scope for the portal? The existing portal row seeds a de row, which no other recent section-map migration does — either deliberate or copy-paste, and the answer decides four vs five language rows.
- Controller/Component naming: `PartnerPortalShops` or `PartnerPortalMerchantAccess`? The latter matches the wiki and  title, the former matches the sidebar label „Obchody".
- An EN section title "Stores" already exists for the cash-register in-store statistics section — confirm „Shop access" as the EN title avoids user-facing confusion.
- Longer term: should `BackendMap` set the `hasSubmenu` flag the template already reads, retiring the hardcoded allowlist? Out of scope here (it would start rendering submenus for every parent across the whole admin), but worth its own ticket.

Note the four-item branded sidebar in this frame is the target portal shell, delivered by follow-up tasks; this task only takes the page title, subtitle and the „Obchody" label from it.
- Migration rules: `migrations/AGENTS.md`
- Page wiring pattern: skill `st-archetype-admin-page-wiring`

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Opus 5, 2026-09-23_

- **The submenu allowlist is the trap in this task.** `admin/templates/navigation.tpl:52` renders a nested `<ul>` only when `in_array($menuItem.id, $triggerSubmenu) || $hasSubmenu`. `$triggerSubmenu` is a hardcoded array of 20 ids at `navigation.tpl:3` and does not contain the Partner Portal row. `$hasSubmenu` is `isset($menuItem.hasSubmenu)` (`:12`) and no PHP anywhere in the repo ever sets that key — verified by grep across `cms/` and `admin/`; it is a dead escape hatch. So adding a child without editing the array produces a parent with no submenu and a child reachable only by typing its URL.
- Referencing section-map ids as literals is established practice, not a hack: `1449`, `1545` and `1779` appear both in `$triggerSubmenu` and in migrations (`migrations/2024/cms/LOG-5764/update_logistics_section_map_drop.sql:20,22`, `migrations/2025/multishop/cms/13318/multishop_routes_renamed_drop.sql`). The Partner Portal row's id is not a literal anywhere yet because `migrations/2026/devrel/cms/CZ3TDR1-542/add_partner_portal_page_drop.sql` inserts it via `LAST_INSERT_ID()` — resolve it per environment before editing the template. Precedent for a parent that is itself a page: id 606 `SectionOverview` („Propojení").
- `admin/templates/navigation.tpl` matches no CODEOWNERS rule (`*.tpl` is not in the `*.css/.less/.js/.ts/.tsx` list at `CODEOWNERS:5-9`, and there is no `/admin/templates` entry). No mandatory reviewer, but the file is shared by every team's menu — keep the diff to the single array.
- The design's „Základní přehled" is not the „Portál partnera" row: it is a hardcoded `<li>` with `{t}Basic Overview{/t}` at `navigation.tpl:92-96`, linking to `BackEndHelper::getAdminHomePageUrl()`. Nothing in this task touches it.
- Today's only portal section-map row: `parentId = 1`, `priority = 550`, slugs `portal-partnera` (cs, sk), `partner-portal` (en, hu), `partnerportal` (de). Omitted columns fall back to schema defaults (`inMenu = 1`, `permissionLevel = 2`, `editableRights = 1`) — `database/schema/st_cms.sql:205-231`.
- `cms2_admin_section_map_lng` has `UNIQUE KEY (language, indexName)`, so slugs are a per-language global namespace. Candidates `vstup-do-obchodu`, `vstup-do-obchodov`, `shop-access`, `belepes-az-uzletekbe`, `shop-zugang` and `obchody` are all unused across `database/migration-zero/st_cms.sql` and `migrations/**` as of 2026-09-23. Convention: kebab-case, localized per language, diacritics stripped (`duse-eshopu` / `dusa-eshopu` / `shop-soul` / `aruhaz-lelke`); a `-cs` / `-sk` / `-en` suffix is used only when the wording is identical across languages.
- Request path: `/admin/{slug}/` → `PageRouterMiddleware::resolvePage()` (`cms/packages/System/Middleware/PageRouterMiddleware.php:66-69`) → `controller` column → `AdminRouter::getControllerClassFromAction()` (`cms/packages/Routing/AdminRouter.php:347-372`, map at `:163`, portal entry at `:298-299`). A missing map entry means the slug resolves to nothing.
- Inertia: the `#[Component]` name must equal the React page directory name (`admin/react/src/index.tsx:146-156`), must be listed in `cms/packages/Inertia/InertiaControllers.php` (portal entry at `:185`), and the props map is generated into `cms/generated/Shoptet/Generated/Inertia/PagePropsMapPaths.php`.
- Menu tree: `parentId` alone decides nesting (`cms/packages/Layout/Model/BackendMap.php:302-337`); sidebar built by `LayoutAdminPackageHelper::getAfterHeaderSectionMap()` (`:473-505`) with `setParentId(1)` and `setLevelLimit(3)`, ordered by `priority, title` (`BackendMap.php:218`). Three levels are allowed, so one level of children is well within limits.
- The module gate is double: `RequiresActiveModule` on the controller (`cms/packages/System/Middleware/ControllerMiddleware.php:117-129`) and `BackendMap`'s active-module filter (`:172-178`). The `partnerPortal` module row itself is defined nowhere in the repo — it is created operationally via `/admin/moduly/`.
- Existing React page is a placeholder: `admin/react/src/PartnerPortal/pages/PartnerPortalOverview/page.tsx:11` — "Placeholder content — the real Partner Portal overview UI lands in follow-up tasks."
- CODEOWNERS (`:514-518`) covers `admin/controllers/PartnerPortal`, `cms/packages/PartnerPortal`, `admin/react/src/PartnerPortal/**` and `config/app/partner-portal-services.neon` — but not `admin/controllers/Props/PartnerPortal*PageProps.php` nor `migrations/2026/devrel/**`.
- No Cypress or PHPUnit coverage exists for the Partner Portal anywhere today.
